topic: How Russia ended up owning a piece of Germany: Königsberg to Kaliningrad

sentences.text: Why does Russia own land between Poland and Lithuania?
It is Kaliningrad, on the Baltic Sea.
Until 1946, it was a German city called Königsberg.
In 1701, a king was crowned in its castle.
In 1944, British bombs burned its old centre.
On 9 April 1945, the Soviets captured it.
At Potsdam, the Allies agreed, in principle, to give it to the Soviets.
Renamed Kaliningrad after Mikhail Kalinin, who was unrelated to it.
Every land link to Russia now crosses NATO and EU.
The full story is on our channel.
sentences.editorial: pointer to the full story on the channel, not a factual claim

claims.claim: In 1944 British bombing attacks burned Königsberg for several days and destroyed its historic centre.

claims.claim: The Soviet Union captured Königsberg on 9 April 1945.

claims.claim: The Potsdam Agreement (section V) says the Conference agreed in principle to the Soviet proposal for the ultimate transfer of the city of Königsberg to the Soviet Union.

claims.claim: Königsberg was renamed Kaliningrad in July 1946 in honour of Mikhail Kalinin, who was unrelated to the city.

claims.claim: All military and civilian land links between the region and the rest of Russia must pass through members of NATO and the EU.
